title: UK fuel duty steps 55.95p to 57.95p/l — the second and final leg of the 5p unwind, restoring the rate frozen from 2011 to 2022
source: EST: gov.uk/government/publications/amended-fuel-duty-rates-for-2026-to-2027/amended-fuel-duty-rates-2026-to-2027 (HM Treasury/HMRC policy paper, first published 2026-05-22T15:28:53+01:00), fetched direct 2026-09-09 via the gov.uk content API (HTTP 200, 21,762 bytes) — its light-oils and heavy-oils tables both carry a 'Rates from 1 March 2027' column reading 0.5795 for unleaded petrol and heavy oil (diesel), against 0.5595 'from 1 January 2027', and the body states 'Fuel Duty rates will then be increased on 1 January 2027 and 1 March 2027 to return them to Fuel Duty levels before March 2022'. Corroborated from the statute book, fetched direct the same day: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/164 article 1(4), as amended by legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/555 article 2(2)(c) (both HTTP 200), gives the intermediate 55.95p tier effect only 'in the period beginning with 1st January 2027 and ending with 28th February 2027' — after which the Order's rebates lapse and the Hydrocarbon Oil Duties Act 1979 s.6 rate of 57.95p applies with no adjustment. Filed estimate for exactly the reasons its 2027-01-01 sibling is: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for HM Treasury, HMRC or the UK statute book, this lane may not self-confirm, and the same gov.uk paper reserves the outcome — 'the government will confirm final rates at Budget 2026' (2026-10-28). Proposed 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research of uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01 LANE, 2026-09-09, and it earns its own slot rather than a footnote for one reason: whether the two steps are decided TOGETHER is itself the open question, and a calendar with only the January leg cannot record the answer. Budget 2025's own announced unwind was STAGED across three dates (1 ppl on 2026-09-01, 2 ppl on 2026-12-01, 2 ppl on 2027-03-01, quoted verbatim in the gov.uk paper above), so a partial resolution at the 2026-10-28 Budget — defer January, keep March, or the reverse — has direct precedent and is not a straw man. That is registered as a falsifiable prediction, FT-uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01-2, scored off the DESNZ weekly duty column. WHAT MAKES THIS LEG DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLING: it is the one that actually ENDS the temporary cut, restoring 57.95p — the rate that stood unchanged from 2011-03-28 to 2022-03-28 in DESNZ's own weekly series. Its ~2.4p pump effect (2p duty plus 20% VAT) lands in the March 2027 CPI collection, published ~2027-04-21, roughly 0.03-0.04pp on headline by the same ONS-weight arithmetic the sibling ledger sets out. It is also the step after which the Budget-2025 plan resumes RPI uprating in future years, so 57.95p is a floor rather than a resting point. Tiered LOW on the same counts as the sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no energy-, rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
